predecessors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: the 1015 shape without its Jaén district: the kingdom 'formed in al-Andalus in 1013' on Granada, before Habbus 'attacked Cabra and Jaén' c.

successors.name: Almoravid dynasty
successors.text: Granada city and its district, 'captured by the Almoravids in September 1090'

ledger.x: 1013: Zawi ibn Ziri founds the Zirid kingdom of Granada.

c. 1028-1029: Habbus pushes north into Jaén. He 'attacked Cabra and Jaén around 1028-1029, expanding north'; the page does not name who held the district, and 'attacked' is read as 'took'. Cliopatria's 1015 outline already contains the district.

c. 1041: Almería is its own master again. The Granada page gives only 'for several years'; the Almería page's rulers list has Ma'n ben Muhammad ben Sumadih from 1041 and a Valencian period ending 1042, so 1041 is a bridge.
1085: Cliopatria narrows Granada to its core.
1090: the independent kingdom of Granada ends; the land passes to the Almoravids (see the loss event).

wars.name: Zirid–Abbadid war of 1036-1039 (Battle of Écija)
wars.outcome: Habbus took Aznalcázar and Tocina and burned Triana in 1036; the Zirids 'defeated the Abbadids of Seville in battle near Écija' in 1039, gaining land to the west.

wars.name: Battle of al-Funt
wars.outcome: Zuhayr of Almería was defeated; the Zirids took much of his land and made Almería a vassal state for several years.

wars.name: Zirid conquest of Málaga
wars.outcome: Badis defeated the Hammudid king of Málaga in battle and annexed his kingdom.

wars.name: Battle of Cabra
wars.outcome: 'The Zirids were defeated in the Battle of Cabra in 1079 against the forces of Seville.'

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Granada
wars.outcome: The Almoravids took Granada in September 1090 without a fight; Abdallah went into exile.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line; the pages name towns (Jaén, Cabra, Aznalcázar, Écija, Málaga, Almería, Granada).
